translation_notes: The loop stays as written: `for track in m{ ?track sstim:martigliPeriodInitial [] }(graph)` for graph.subjects(P, None) (the blank node is the non-projected wildcard), then one `m{ {track} P ?x }(graph).first()` per `next(graph.objects(track, P), None)`. The three reads are NOT fused into one join: the original consumes the first value of each predicate only, a join reaches every combination.

SSTIM and local() are module-level helpers from generate-hed-bundle.py (lines 70, 109-111) not visible in the extracted region: restored directly in original.py/translated.ldpy since they are one-liners, no separate shim file needed

Four calls: fixture.ttl (one sweep among neighbours, with other properties of the same subject before the three read), fixture_multivalued.ttl (multi-valued predicates), fixture_order.ttl (two sweeps met in store order, not written order, behind an incomplete track) and an empty graph. Both sides walk graph.triples() in the same order (m{ } is a nested loop over triples, record ldpy/016), so the first sweep returned is the same on both sides.

Repair 2026-10-30: the first translation fused the three reads into one three-pattern m{ }, which differs when a predicate is multi-valued (fixture_multivalued.ttl: original {'track': 't2', ...} against {'track': 't1', 'mp0': 4.0, 'mp1': 3.0, 'md': 0.5}); retranslated read by read with .first(), which is what INSTRUCTIONS.md §2 requires when the code consumes only the first value.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: each `next(graph.objects(track, P), None)` becomes `graph.value(track, P)` (rdflib's value() returns the first object or None, any=True by default); the two guards are merged into `if None in (mp0, mp1, md) or float(mp0) == float(mp1): continue`; the returned dict is written on one line. The outer subjects() loop stays: replacing it by subject_objects() would read the per-triple value instead of the first, which fixture_multivalued.ttl tells apart.
